item.title: Artificial Intelligence: Covert Testing Used Common Platforms to Create Viable Attack Plans
item.description:
What GAO Found
In spring 2026, GAO’s prompts to four of the most used generative artificial intelligence (AI) platforms–Claude, Grok, ChatGPT, and Gemini—produced feasible information that could assist a malicious actor with planning and executing attacks. Specifically, in response to prompts, two platforms produced information for constructing and detonating an improvised explosive device (IED) designed to cause mass casualties. In addition, after prompting, two other platforms produced information for targeting the electrical grid with a drone and firearms, respectively, to cause economic harm. Each of these platforms provided detailed information that could be used to carry out attacks, such as specific targets, locations, timing, and attack methods. Each platform took less than 12 hours to generate the attack plans; however, the amount of time to get results could vary for many reasons, including the topic and user experience. In each case, GAO’s prompts triggered the platforms’ safeguards, such as denial, removal of information, or suspending accounts. GAO was able to circumvent those safeguards by using common safeguard-bypassing techniques. GAO verified the viability of the information through research, surveillance, and interviews with experts. Why GAO Did This Study
Generative AI is dramatically increasing productivity and decreasing the time it takes to perform many tasks. These advancements are enabling malicious actors to pursue nefarious actions faster and more efficiently and empowering less-skilled individuals by filling knowledge gaps through providing detailed expertise in sensitive areas. There is a risk that generative AI could be misused to successfully complete malicious acts, such as producing harmful content, disclosing sensitive information, or carrying out other instructions that defy the AI’s intended purposes and built-in safeguards.
GAO was asked to review issues related to the malicious use of AI. This report describes how commercially available AI can be used for malicious purposes to exacerbate national security risks and cause economic harm.
To address this objective, through discussions with experts, GAO selected two scenarios in which AI could be used maliciously to: (1) facilitate the construction of an IED causing mass casualties and risks to national security and (2) facilitate an attack on the electrical grid causing economic harm. Using usage statistics, GAO identified the four most-used generative AI platforms as of April 2026 (i.e., Claude, Grok, ChatGPT, and Gemini) and randomly assigned each to a scenario and an alphabetic character to present the results. GAO submitted prompts to each platform to obtain information and collaborated with experts on which parts of the plans could be safely validated and verified the viability of the information. GAO also interviewed officials from the four companies associated with each of the platforms.
Officials from the companies generally stated that their companies will continue to improve the safety of their platforms.
For more information, contact Kevin Walsh April Gamble GambleA@gao.gov at WalshK@gao.gov.
